briefdescription.para: This function demonstrates a multi-block SHAKE256 XOF (extendable-output function) squeeze.

detaileddescription.para: It absorbs the 'HELLO' string once and then squeezes ASU_SHAKE256_XOF_OUTPUT_LEN bytes of output across multiple 136-byte rate blocks by issuing repeated FINISH requests through XAsu_Sha3Operation() with XofEnableFlag set on every block except the last. The SHA3 engine is kept alive between blocks, and the same client priority is reused so the same context (and hence the same engine) is retained across the squeeze. A failed server FINISH already releases the engine on ASUFW. If the client cannot send a request after a successful continuation, ASUFW reclaim/timeout releases the held engine.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS, if the multi-block SHAKE256 XOF squeeze completes successfully.
XST_FAILURE, if the squeeze fails.//! [SHAKE256 XOF example]

inbodydescription.para: Common client request inputs. The same priority is reused for every block so that the same context (and hence the same SHA3 engine) is retained across the squeeze.
All squeeze blocks run in SHA3 SHAKE256 mode.

Squeeze the output in 136-byte rate blocks. The first block also absorbs the message (INIT | UPDATE | FINISH); subsequent blocks are FINISH-only continuations. The final block (IsLastHashBlock = TRUE) may be shorter than a full rate block and releases the engine.
Request another block on every squeeze except the last.
The first block (Offset == 0) also absorbs the message; the rest are FINISH-only.
Wait for the response of this block before issuing the next squeeze.
Verify the squeezed output against the known-answer SHAKE256 XOF of the 'HELLO' string.
